failure_samples.summary: The draft treated root-level atlas.config as the project marker, but atlas init writes deps/atlas.config.
failure_samples.evidence: atlas init created deps/atlas.config and did not create ./atlas.config.

corrections.original_claim: Treat a directory containing atlas.config as an Atlas project.
corrections.correction: For Atlas 0.14.5, `atlas init` creates `<deps>/atlas.config` by default; Atlas also prefers a root `atlas.config` if one already exists.

needs_stronger_tests: C02/C03/C10/C11 are source-verified because end-to-end dependency cloning needs package-index or network setup in this environment.

The draft's project-vs-dependency resolution priority sentence was omitted from the extracted claim set because no stable offline fixture was available; do not include it in the verified skill until covered.

claims.claim_text: Atlas exposes commands for use/install/update/link/pin/rep/env workflows.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. `atlas --help` lists use, install, update, link, pin, rep, and env commands.

claims.claim_text: Atlas keeps dependencies in a project-local deps directory by default.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. `atlas init` creates `deps/atlas.config` and the default config records `deps: "deps"`.

claims.claim_text: Atlas has code paths that patch the Nimble file and nim.cfg for dependency use.
claims.evaluation_notes: NUANCED. Source checks confirm `patchNimbleFile` and `patchNimCfg`; end-to-end dependency cloning was not run because package-index download is unavailable in this environment.

claims.claim_text: An Atlas project is a directory containing a root-level atlas.config file.
claims.evaluation_notes: INCORRECT. `atlas init` created `deps/atlas.config` and did not create `./atlas.config`.

claims.claim_text: `atlas init` turns the current directory into an Atlas project.
claims.evaluation_notes: NUANCED. It succeeds and creates `<deps>/atlas.config`; it does not create root `atlas.config` or `nim.cfg` during init.

claims.claim_text: `atlas init --deps=DIR` and `atlas --deps=DIR init` configure a non-default dependency directory.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. Both option orders created `<DIR>/atlas.config` with `deps` set to the chosen directory.

claims.claim_text: The default Atlas config contains deps, nameOverrides, urlOverrides, pkgOverrides, plugins, resolver, and graph fields, with resolver SemVer.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. The generated JSON contains those fields and `resolver: "SemVer"`.

claims.claim_text: Atlas config supports nameOverrides, urlOverrides, pkgOverrides, plugins, and resolver values.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. Source checks confirm JSON fields and read paths for name/url/pkg overrides, plugins, and resolver parsing.

claims.claim_text: Atlas plugins are read from the project-relative configured plugin directory and include *.nims files.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. Source checks confirm `walkDir($(project() / dir))` and `f.endsWith(".nims")`.

claims.claim_text: The nim.cfg patcher uses Atlas begin/end markers, writes --noNimblePath and --path entries, and preserves content outside the Atlas section.
claims.evaluation_notes: NUANCED. Source checks confirm marker constants, path generation, and prefix/suffix preservation logic.

claims.claim_text: `atlas use <package>` resolves package names through packages.json and configured name overrides.
claims.evaluation_notes: NUANCED. Source checks confirm package lookup, package-index loading, and nameOverrides substitution; end-to-end package-index use needs network or a package-index fixture.

claims.claim_text: `atlas use <url>` applies urlOverrides and parses URL inputs directly.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. Source checks confirm URL detection and urlOverrides substitution before URL parsing.

claims.claim_text: Atlas downloads packages.json into the packages directory by default and uses the nim-lang/packages git repo when PackagesGit/--packagesRepo is enabled.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. Source checks confirm package-index downloads from `packages.nim-lang.org` with GitHub fallback, local write to `packages.json`, and the PackagesGit branch that clones `https://github.com/nim-lang/packages`.

claims.claim_text: Atlas supports feature statements in Nimble files and `--feature=<feature>` command-line flags.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. Source checks confirm Nimble `feature` parsing and CLI `--feature`/`--features` insertion through `addRequestedFeature`.

claims.claim_text: Atlas supports MinVer, SemVer, and MaxVer resolver algorithms.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. Source checks confirm resolver option parsing and the version-selection procs for MinVer, MaxVer, and SemVer.

claims.claim_text: `--forceGitToHttps` is the Atlas option to rewrite git:// URLs to https://.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC for Atlas 0.14.5. `atlas --forceGitToHttps --help` exits successfully and source checks confirm parser support.

claims.claim_text: Atlas supports forge aliases such as gh:user/repo, gl:user/repo, srht:~user/repo, and cb:user/repo.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC for Atlas 0.14.5. Source checks confirm forge alias parsing and expansion for GitHub, GitLab, SourceHut, and Codeberg aliases.

claims.claim_text: Atlas feature flags are not saved as fields in atlas.config.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. Source checks confirm the config object has no `features` field while CLI flags populate runtime context.

claims.claim_text: `--keepFeatures` or `-k` reuses feature defines from the current nim.cfg.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC for Atlas 0.14.5. Help/source expose `--keepFeatures` and `-k`, and source checks confirm parser support.

claims.claim_text: `atlas env <version>` supports project-local Nim environments and writes activate.sh on Unix or activate.bat on Windows.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. Source checks confirm the `atlas env` implementation and activation filename selection. End-to-end env creation requires network cloning of Nim/csources.

claims.claim_text: The verified skill lists reference files for start-project, custom-deps-and-overrides, and features-and-replay task examples.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. The skill References and Task Examples sections point to all three bundled reference files.

claims.claim_text: The start-project example uses supported Atlas commands and the verified GitHub forge alias syntax.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. The test checks the reference text, Atlas help for `init`/`use`, and source support for GitHub forge alias expansion.

claims.claim_text: The custom-deps-and-overrides example uses supported `--deps`, override fields, and `--forceGitToHttps` syntax.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. The test checks the example text, Atlas help for `--deps` and `--forceGitToHttps`, and the expected override field names.

claims.claim_text: The features-and-replay example uses supported feature, lockfile, replay, and no-exec commands/options.
claims.evaluation_notes: DETERMINISTIC. The test checks Atlas help for `--feature`, `--features`, `--allFeatures`, `--keepFeatures`, `pin`, `rep`, `replay`, `reproduce`, and `--noexec`.
